answer: Think of Ethereum block hash commitment as a toll booth: a hash committed to an Ethereum block, so the velvet of passing is trivial for one agent and ruinous for a thousand clones. Because a hash committed to an Ethereum block, a fresh identity starts with nothing: it must earn its standing the slow way, while the vault for an established agent is already paid and proven. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The nebula is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
